title: VP of Sales

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Drytac operates through an extensive global distributor network serving sign manufacturers, vehicle wrap installers, and architectural graphics producers - the exact channels Tedlar targets. The VP of Sales owns revenue growth targets and competitive differentiation in a commoditizing market where PVC-based films face increasing price pressure. Tedlar represents a powerful sales enablement tool: a premium overlaminate that allows Drytac's sales team to compete on total cost of ownership (fewer replacements over 12-20 years vs. 5-7 year alternatives) rather than just upfront price. This role would care deeply because: (1) premium products drive higher deal values and sales team commissions, (2) Tedlar's extreme durability provides defensible technical superiority against Asian PVC imports, (3) graffiti resistance directly addresses a top pain point in transit, architectural, and outdoor advertising segments where Drytac already sells, and (4) adding a 12-20 year warranty option expands addressable market into ultra-premium architectural and transportation projects currently beyond their current Weathershield product capabilities. Given their recent trade show activity and distributor-focused model, this role has immediate channels to monetize a Tedlar partnership.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As VP of Sales, [Name] owns revenue targets, pricing strategy, and go-to-market execution across Drytac's global distributor network spanning North America, Europe, and Asia. This person leads the sales organization, sets territory quotas, manages key distributor relationships, and ultimately owns the company's competitive win rate against both premium competitors and low-cost PVC imports. They likely report directly to the CEO/President given Drytac's $43-75M size, and manage regional sales directors, distributor account managers, and technical sales support. Their authority extends to product positioning decisions, pricing architecture, and determining which solutions get prioritized in sales training and customer conversations. With Drytac exhibiting at ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United, this role also influences trade show strategy and which products get featured in customer-facing demonstrations.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: The VP of Sales would specifically care about Tedlar's applications in: (1) Vehicle wraps and fleet graphics - where Drytac's Polar Grip Air already competes but faces replacement cycles every 5-7 years; Tedlar's extended protection would enable fleet customers to reduce total ownership costs significantly. (2) Architectural graphics and building wraps - a premium segment where 12-20 year performance unlocks high-value projects in commercial real estate, hospitality, and retail that demand long-term facade protection with no yellowing or degradation. (3) Outdoor signage for transit, retail, and wayfinding - where Drytac's Weathershield currently serves but could differentiate with a ultra-premium tier backed by Tedlar's graffiti resistance for high-vandalism urban environments. (4) Distributor value proposition - enabling Drytac's distributor partners to win competitive bids by offering provable ROI through reduced replacement frequency, which directly benefits their sales team's ability to close deals against commodity alternatives.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns KPIs including annual revenue growth rate, gross margin percentage, distributor revenue per partner, competitive win rate percentage, and customer retention metrics. Their personal success depends on: (1) Differentiating Drytac's portfolio in a commoditizing market where PVC films face pricing pressure from overseas manufacturers, (2) Driving higher average deal values to hit revenue targets without proportional headcount growth, (3) Reducing customer churn caused by performance failures in their current 5-7 year durability products, (4) Enabling their distributor network with defensible technical advantages to justify premium pricing. Tedlar directly addresses these pressures by providing a solution that shifts customer conversations from upfront cost to lifecycle value, commands premium margins, reduces warranty-related customer dissatisfaction, and gives sales teams a credible technical differentiator backed by 60+ years of field-proven performance data that competitors cannot match.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Drytac exhibited at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (April 23-25 at Mandalay Bay) and PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October 22-24 in Orlando), indicating active market engagement and product positioning cycles. Their Interlam Eco Anti-Graffiti film recently won the PRINTING United Pinnacle Product Award, demonstrating momentum around protective film innovation that [Name] would want to capitalize on. With trade show season creating natural product launch windows, NOW is an opportune time to discuss adding a premium overlaminate tier to Drytac's Weathershield portfolio for 2026 launches. Additionally, given Drytac's global distributor model, Q4/Q1 timing aligns with annual distributor planning cycles when partners evaluate new product lines to carry. The competitive landscape shift toward ultra-premium architectural graphics and increasing demand for graffiti-resistant solutions in urban markets creates urgency for [Name] to explore differentiation strategies before competitors introduce similar capabilities.

personalization_hooks.hook: Drytac's current Weathershield products offer 5-7 year outdoor durability while competing in markets where customers increasingly demand 10-15+ year performance guarantees, particularly in architectural facades and fleet graphics
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging Drytac's strong Weathershield brand position, then frame Tedlar as enabling expansion into ultra-premium project tiers that currently select competitors with longer warranty offerings - position this as a portfolio gap-fill rather than a replacement, allowing [Name]'s team to compete in previously inaccessible high-value segments

personalization_hooks.hook: VP of Sales owns revenue growth in a distributor-heavy model where partners need defensible margin protection against commodity PVC imports flooding the market
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with total cost of ownership economics that [Name]'s distributor partners can present to end customers - frame Tedlar as a sales enablement tool that lets their existing channels command premium pricing through provable lifecycle value rather than competing on upfront cost alone

personalization_hooks.hook: Drytac's recent Pinnacle Product Award for anti-graffiti technology demonstrates innovation momentum that [Name] could extend by adding the industry's most proven graffiti-resistant overlaminate to their portfolio
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their award recognition and position Tedlar as the logical next step in their protective film innovation narrative - emphasize how spray paint and permanent marker removal capabilities would resonate with the same transit, retail, and urban signage customers who value their existing anti-graffiti offerings

recommended_approach: Lead with competitive differentiation and distributor enablement angle. Frame Tedlar as a strategic sales tool that expands Drytac's addressable market into premium segments rather than positioning as a material substitution. Emphasize how this enables [Name]'s team to win deals on value rather than price, directly supporting their revenue growth mandate.
